section: Iterate - change: test hardening for CRLF fixtures and leads e2e guard
title: Guard e2e specs against touching a real ~/.claude/leads and normalise fixture EOL in tests
context: 5 W1 server tests failed on Windows autocrlf checkouts (CRLF fixtures), and 15 Org/Lead Playwright specs seeded and deleted ~/.claude/leads with no check that HOME is isolated.
decision: Tests LF-normalise fixture reads (no .gitattributes change). One helper e2e/helpers/leads-home-guard.ts (guardedLeadsRoot, removeLeadsPath) requires SHIPWRIGHT_E2E_ISOLATED=1 and a HOME strictly under a non-root temp dir; all specs use it; a vitest source-scan ratchet fails on bare rm of a leads path.
consequences: Running a leads spec outside isolated-stack now throws at module load. SHIPWRIGHT_LEADS_ROOT overrides must point inside the isolated HOME. The ratchet is lexical (wrapper parameters are not traced); the runtime guard is the real protection.
rationale: Guard writes as well as deletes (code review high): root is taken at spec load. Doubts answered: tmpdir root and missing marker now refuse; realpath errors propagate; scan covers mjs/js, aliases, shell rm. Rebutted: corpus replace is a harmless no-op kept per brief; guard not merged with temp-dir.ts (stricter strict-child semantics).
rejected: A .gitattributes eol=lf rule for the fixtures: sensitive path that blocks the PR Review gate.
